# S337 — wave start launches without --yes when stdin is not a terminal

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-11** — Correction 2026-11-11: the slices were NOT launched. The run in the ledger (run-20261111-170605-e94e) held only a spec-check step, which ended pass at 17:07:58; the CLI was killed by the 60 s timeout before any launch. So the observed problem is narrower: without --yes and with stdin from /dev/null, `ork wave start` starts and records a spec-check run (a model call) before any confirmation and prints nothing while it runs. Expected: print the plan first, and run nothing that costs a model call until confirmed, or say on stderr that a spec check is running.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**2026-11-20** — `ork wave start` with no --yes, --questions or --answer on input that is not a terminal prints the plans and a `not started:` line, exits 2 and runs no spec check; the doc findings from review are fixed and the full suite, vet, gofmt and slicer check are green.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Observed 2026-11-11 (slicer wave): `ork wave start slicer s454 s455 s450 s456 s451 --implementer claude:sonnet:high --reviewer grok:grok-4.7:medium --architect off </dev/null` (no --yes) printed nothing for 60 s and was killed by timeout; `ork status` then showed run-20261111-170605-e94e active with a spec-check running. The same command before the project had a check command printed the plan and refused. Expected: without --yes and with no terminal to confirm on, print the plan and exit without launching (or refuse), never launch silently.

Re-anchored 2026-11-18:

- Fixed since: the CLI now prints `spec check: reading ITEMS (it runs even with --well-specified)` before the spec check call (S264; `internal/cli/wave.go:551-552`, `TestWaveStartSaysToWaitForTheSpecCheck`). Piped spec answers are refused (S404, adj 452 `cli.spec-answers`; `internal/cli/wave.go:675-700`). `--questions` and `--answer` exist for a caller with no terminal (S312; `internal/cli/wave.go:848-864`).
- Still open: `startWave` plans every item, then runs the spec check (a model call, `daemon.MethodSpecCheck`, `internal/cli/wave.go:381-382`), and only then asks "Start this wave?" (`internal/cli/wave.go:416-421`). With stdin at EOF the confirm reads an empty line and fails with "Start this wave? requires y or n" (exit 2, `internal/cli/wave.go:321-333`). So a caller with no terminal and no `--yes` always pays for a spec check that cannot lead to a start.
- ork already tells a terminal from a pipe or /dev/null: `App.terminal` (`internal/cli/specdraft.go:35-50`, with the `App.Terminal` test hook at `internal/cli/cli.go:306`).
- `ork run` has the same order (spec check at `internal/cli/run.go:143`, confirm at `internal/cli/run.go:163-166`). This slice covers `ork wave start` only, as its title says; `ork run` is noted for a later item.

This slice touches `internal/cli` output, so it gets a UI pass (rule u10).

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests and see the first one red for the stated reason; the other three are green guards.
2. `startWave`: after the plans are printed and the pair rule is checked, and before `a.specCheck`, when `!opts.yes && !opts.spec.active() && !a.terminal()`, print the `not started:` line to the prompts writer and return `ExitUsage`. With `--json`, print `{"started": false, "held": [], "no_spec": []}` (the `notStarted` shape) on stdout first.
3. Leave `ork run` unchanged.
4. Docs: `docs/guide.md` (a caller without a terminal passes `--yes`, or `--questions` then `--answer`), `docs/design.md` CLI section. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S337 --text "..."`.
